claim: Thermodynamic models of gene regulation can predict transcriptional regulation in bacteria.
source: Thermodynamic models of gene regulation can predict transcriptional regulation in bacteria, but in eukaryotes, chromatin accessibility and energy expenditure may call for a different framework.
evidence: Supported by references to prior work on bacterial systems

claim: In eukaryotes, chromatin accessibility and energy expenditure may call for a different framework than thermodynamic models.
source: Thermodynamic models of gene regulation can predict transcriptional regulation in bacteria, but in eukaryotes, chromatin accessibility and energy expenditure may call for a different framework.
evidence: Stated as motivation for the study

claim: The study systematically tested the predictive power of models of DNA accessibility based on the Monod-Wyman-Changeux (MWC) model of allostery.
source: Here, we systematically tested the predictive power of models of DNA accessibility based on the Monod-Wyman-Changeux (MWC) model of allostery, which posits that chromatin fluctuates between accessible and inaccessible states.
evidence: Description of the experimental approach taken

claim: The MWC model posits that chromatin fluctuates between accessible and inaccessible states.
source: Here, we systematically tested the predictive power of models of DNA accessibility based on the Monod-Wyman-Changeux (MWC) model of allostery, which posits that chromatin fluctuates between accessible and inaccessible states.
evidence: Definition of the MWC model framework

claim: The study dissected the regulatory dynamics of hunchback by the activator Bicoid and the pioneer-like transcription factor Zelda in living Drosophila embryos.
source: We dissected the regulatory dynamics of hunchback by the activator Bicoid and the pioneer-like transcription factor Zelda in living Drosophila embryos and showed that no thermodynamic or non-equilibrium MWC model can recapitulate hunchback transcription.
evidence: Description of experimental measurements performed

claim: No thermodynamic or non-equilibrium MWC model can recapitulate hunchback transcription.
source: We dissected the regulatory dynamics of hunchback by the activator Bicoid and the pioneer-like transcription factor Zelda in living Drosophila embryos and showed that no thermodynamic or non-equilibrium MWC model can recapitulate hunchback transcription.
evidence: Main finding from systematic model testing

claim: DNA accessibility is catalyzed by Bicoid and Zelda, possibly through histone acetylation.
source: Therefore, we explored a model where DNA accessibility is not the result of thermal fluctuations but is catalyzed by Bicoid and Zelda, possibly through histone acetylation, and found that this model can predict hunchback dynamics.
evidence: Proposed mechanism based on model fitting and literature

claim: A model where DNA accessibility is catalyzed by Bicoid and Zelda can predict hunchback dynamics.
source: Therefore, we explored a model where DNA accessibility is not the result of thermal fluctuations but is catalyzed by Bicoid and Zelda, possibly through histone acetylation, and found that this model can predict hunchback dynamics.
evidence: Result from model fitting to experimental data

claim: Thermodynamic models use equilibrium statistical mechanics to calculate the probability of finding transcription factors bound to DNA.
source: This challenge has been met with a plethora of theoretical works, including thermodynamic models, which use equilibrium statistical mechanics to calculate the probability of finding transcription factors bound to DNA and to relate this probability to the output rate of mRNA production (Ackers et al., 1982; Buchler et al., 2003; Vilar and Leibler, 2003; Bolouri and Davidson, 2003; Bintu et al., 2005a; Bintu et al., 2005b; Sherman and Cohen, 2012).
evidence: Definition of thermodynamic models with citations

claim: Thermodynamic models relate the probability of transcription factor binding to the output rate of mRNA production.
source: This challenge has been met with a plethora of theoretical works, including thermodynamic models, which use equilibrium statistical mechanics to calculate the probability of finding transcription factors bound to DNA and to relate this probability to the output rate of mRNA production (Ackers et al., 1982; Buchler et al., 2003; Vilar and Leibler, 2003; Bolouri and Davidson, 2003; Bintu et al., 2005a; Bintu et al., 2005b; Sherman and Cohen, 2012).
evidence: Definition of thermodynamic models with citations

claim: Thermodynamic models of bacterial transcription have largely confirmed their predictive power for several operons.
source: Thermodynamic models of bacterial transcription launched a dialogue between theory and experiments that has largely confirmed their predictive power for several operons (Ackers et al., 1982; Bakk et al., 2004; Zeng et al., 2010; He et al., 2010; Garcia and Phillips, 2011; Brewster et al., 2012; Cui et al., 2013; Brewster et al., 2014; Sepúlveda et al., 2016; Razo-Mejia et al., 2018) with a few potential exceptions (Garcia et al., 2012; Hammar et al., 2014).
evidence: Summary of prior work with citations

claim: Thermodynamic models have been widely applied to eukaryotes to describe transcriptional regulation in yeast, human cells, and Drosophila melanogaster.
source: Following these successes, thermodynamic models have been widely applied to eukaryotes to describe transcriptional regulation in yeast (Segal et al., 2006; Gertz et al., 2009; Sharon et al., 2012; Zeigler and Cohen, 2014), human cells (Giorgetti et al., 2010), and the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster (Jaeger et al., 2004a; Zinzen et al., 2006; Segal et al., 2008; Fakhouri et al., 2010; Parker et al., 2011; Kanodia et al., 2012; White et al., 2012; Samee et al., 2015; Sayal et al., 2016).
evidence: Summary of prior applications with citations

claim: In eukaryotes, DNA is tightly packed in nucleosomes and must become accessible in order for transcription factor binding and transcription to occur.
source: First, in eukaryotes, DNA is tightly packed in nucleosomes and must become accessible in order for transcription factor binding and transcription to occur (Polach and Widom, 1995; Levine, 2010; Schulze and Wallrath, 2007; Lam et al., 2008; Raveh-Sadka et al., 2009; Li et al., 2011; Fussner et al., 2011; Bai et al., 2011; Li et al., 2014b; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015).
evidence: Established biological knowledge with citations

claim: The equilibrium framework may be insufficient to account for the energy-expending steps involved in eukaryotic transcriptional regulation.
source: Second, recent reports have speculated that, unlike in bacteria, the equilibrium framework may be insufficient to account for the energy-expending steps involved in eukaryotic transcriptional regulation, such as histone modifications and nucleosome remodeling, calling for non-equilibrium models of transcriptional regulation (Kim and O'Shea, 2008; Estrada et al., 2016; Li et al., 2018; Park et al., 2019).
evidence: Speculation from cited literature

claim: The thermodynamic MWC model assumes that chromatin rapidly transitions between accessible and inaccessible states via thermal fluctuations.
source: This thermodynamic MWC model assumes that chromatin rapidly transitions between accessible and inaccessible states via thermal fluctuations, and that the binding of transcription factors to accessible DNA shifts this equilibrium toward the accessible state.
evidence: Definition of model assumptions

claim: The binding of transcription factors to accessible DNA shifts the equilibrium toward the accessible state in the thermodynamic MWC model.
source: This thermodynamic MWC model assumes that chromatin rapidly transitions between accessible and inaccessible states via thermal fluctuations, and that the binding of transcription factors to accessible DNA shifts this equilibrium toward the accessible state.
evidence: Definition of model mechanism

claim: In thermodynamic models, the transitions between states are assumed to be much faster than both the rate of transcriptional initiation and changes in transcription factor concentrations.
source: Additionally, in all thermodynamic models, the transitions between states are assumed to be much faster than both the rate of transcriptional initiation and changes in transcription factor concentrations.
evidence: Definition of separation of time scales assumption

claim: The separation of time scales, combined with a lack of energy dissipation, makes it possible to consider the states to be in equilibrium such that the probability of each state can be computed using its Boltzmann weight.
source: This separation of time scales, combined with a lack of energy dissipation in the process of regulation, makes it possible to consider the states to be in equilibrium such that the probability of each state can be computed using its Boltzmann weight (Garcia et al., 2007).
evidence: Explanation of thermodynamic model framework with citation

claim: Non-equilibrium models maintain the occupancy hypothesis but make no assumptions about separation of time scales or energy expenditure.
source: Indeed, Narula and Igoshin, 2010, Hammar et al., 2014, Estrada et al., 2016, Scholes et al., 2017, and Li et al., 2018 have proposed theoretical treatments of transcriptional regulation that maintain the occupancy hypothesis, but make no assumptions about separation of time scales or energy expenditure in the process of regulation.
evidence: Description of alternative modeling approaches with citations

claim: Neither the thermodynamic MWC model nor the non-equilibrium MWC model have been tested experimentally in eukaryotic transcriptional regulation.
source: To our knowledge, neither the thermodynamic MWC model nor the non-equilibrium MWC model have been tested experimentally in eukaryotic transcriptional regulation.
evidence: Statement of knowledge gap

claim: The hunchback gene is activated in a step-like manner by the Bicoid activator and the pioneer-like transcription factor Zelda.
source: Here, we performed a systematic dissection of the predictive power of these MWC models of DNA allostery in the embryonic development of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster in the context of the step-like activation of the hunchback gene by the Bicoid activator and the pioneer-like transcription factor Zelda (Driever et al., 1989; Nien et al., 2011; Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: Description of biological system with citations

claim: The hunchback P2 minimal enhancer is believed to be devoid of significant input signals other than activation by Bicoid and regulation of chromatin accessibility by both Bicoid and Zelda during the first 2 hr of embryonic development.
source: During the first 2 hr of embryonic development, the hunchback P2 minimal enhancer (Margolis et al., 1995; Driever et al., 1989; Perry et al., 2012; Park et al., 2019) is believed to be devoid of significant input signals other than activation by Bicoid and regulation of chromatin accessibility by both Bicoid and Zelda (Perry et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2014; Hannon et al., 2017).
evidence: Description of regulatory context with citations

claim: The early regulation of hunchback provides an ideal scaffold for a stringent test of simple theoretical models of eukaryotic transcriptional regulation.
source: As a result, the early regulation of hunchback provides an ideal scaffold for a stringent test of simple theoretical models of eukaryotic transcriptional regulation.
evidence: Justification for choice of experimental system

claim: In the thermodynamic MWC model implementation for hunchback, in the inaccessible state, neither Bicoid nor Zelda can bind DNA.
source: Our implementation of the thermodynamic MWC model (Figure 1A) in the context of hunchback states that in the inaccessible state, neither Bicoid nor Zelda can bind DNA.
evidence: Model assumption stated explicitly

claim: In the accessible state, DNA is unwrapped and the binding sites become accessible to Bicoid and Zelda.
source: In the accessible state, DNA is unwrapped and the binding sites become accessible to these transcription factors.
evidence: Model assumption stated explicitly

claim: The binding of Bicoid or Zelda can shift the equilibrium toward the accessible state.
source: However, the binding of Bicoid or Zelda can shift the equilibrium toward the accessible state (Adams and Workman, 1995; Miller and Widom, 2003; Mirny, 2010; Narula and Igoshin, 2010; Marzen et al., 2013).
evidence: Model mechanism with citations

claim: The model assumes that all binding sites for a given molecular species have the same binding affinity.
source: In our model, we assume that all binding sites for a given molecular species have the same binding affinity.
evidence: Model assumption stated explicitly

claim: Relaxing the assumption that all binding sites have the same affinity does not affect the conclusions.
source: Relaxing this assumption does not affect any of our conclusions (as we will see below in Sections 'The thermodynamic MWC model fails to predict activation of hunchback in the absence of Zelda' and 'No thermodynamic model can recapitulate the activation of hunchback by Bicoid alone').
evidence: Statement about robustness of conclusions

claim: There is no evidence of direct interaction between Zelda and any other proteins.
source: However, since to our knowledge there is no evidence of direct interaction between Zelda and any other proteins, we assume no interaction between Zelda and Bicoid, or between Zelda and RNAP.
evidence: Statement about lack of evidence leading to model assumption

claim: The actual model accounts for at least 6 Bicoid-binding sites and 10 Zelda-binding sites that have been identified within the hunchback P2 enhancer.
source: Note that the actual model utilized throughout this work accounts for at least 6 Bicoid-binding sites and 10 Zelda-binding sites that have been identified within the hunchback P2 enhancer (Section 'Predicting Zelda binding sites'; Driever and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1988; Driever and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1989; Park et al., 2019).
evidence: Model specification based on known binding sites with citations

claim: Embryonic development is a highly dynamic process in which the concentrations of transcription factors are constantly changing.
source: However, embryonic development is a highly dynamic process in which the concentrations of transcription factors are constantly changing due to their nuclear import and export dynamics, and due to protein production, diffusion, and degradation (Edgar and Schubiger, 1986; Edgar et al., 1987; Jaeger et al., 2004b; Gregor et al., 2007b).
evidence: Description of biological context with citations

claim: It is necessary to go beyond steady-state assumptions and to predict and measure how the instantaneous, time-varying concentrations of Bicoid and Zelda at each point in space dictate hunchback output transcriptional dynamics.
source: As a result, it is necessary to go beyond steady-state assumptions and to predict and measure how the instantaneous, time-varying concentrations of Bicoid and Zelda at each point in space dictate hunchback output transcriptional dynamics.
evidence: Methodological requirement stated

claim: The Bicoid-eGFP line displays the exponential Bicoid gradient across the length of the embryo.
source: As expected, this line displayed the exponential Bicoid gradient across the length of the embryo (Appendix section 2.1; Appendix 1—figure 3B).
evidence: Experimental observation consistent with prior knowledge

claim: After anaphase and nuclear envelope formation, the Bicoid nuclear concentration quickly increases as a result of nuclear import.
source: As previously reported (Gregor et al., 2007b), after anaphase and nuclear envelope formation, the Bicoid nuclear concentration quickly increases as a result of nuclear import.
evidence: Experimental observation with citation

claim: The Zelda concentration is spatially uniform along the embryo.
source: Consistent with previous results (Staudt et al., 2006; Liang et al., 2008; Dufourt et al., 2018), the Zelda concentration was spatially uniform along the embryo (Appendix 1—figure 3).
evidence: Experimental observation with citations

claim: The overall concentration dynamics of both Bicoid and Zelda are qualitatively comparable.
source: Contrasting Figure 3A and B reveals that the overall concentration dynamics of both Bicoid and Zelda are qualitatively comparable.
evidence: Observation from comparing experimental data

claim: The high reproducibility of the concentration dynamics of Bicoid and Zelda allows combining measurements from multiple embryos by synchronizing their anaphase to create an 'averaged embryo'.
source: Given the high reproducibility of the concentration dynamics of Bicoid and Zelda (Appendix 1—figure 3), we combined measurements from multiple embryos by synchronizing their anaphase in order to create an 'averaged embryo' (Appendix section 2.1), an approach that has been repeatedly used to describe protein and transcriptional dynamics in the early fly embryo (Garcia et al., 2013; Bothma et al., 2014; Bothma et al., 2015; Berrocal et al., 2018; Lammers et al., 2020).
evidence: Methodological approach justified by data reproducibility and citations

claim: The model assumes that hunchback output depends on the instantaneous concentration of input transcription factors.
source: Our model assumes that hunchback output depends on the instantaneous concentration of input transcription factors.
evidence: Model assumption stated explicitly

claim: The MS2 system results in the fluorescent labeling of sites of nascent transcript formation.
source: Here, 24 repeats of the MS2 loop are inserted in the 5′ untranslated region of the hunchback P2 reporter (Garcia et al., 2013), resulting in the fluorescent labeling of sites of nascent transcript formation (Figure 4A; Video 3).
evidence: Description of experimental method with citation

claim: MS2 fluorescence is proportional to the number of RNAP molecules actively transcribing the gene.
source: This fluorescence is proportional to the number of RNAP molecules actively transcribing the gene (Garcia et al., 2013).
evidence: Relationship between measurement and biological quantity with citation

claim: The experimental mean fluorescence as a function of time is in qualitative agreement with the theoretical prediction.
source: The experimental mean fluorescence as a function of time measured in a narrow window (2.5% of the total embryo length, averaged across nuclei in the window) along the length of the embryo (Figure 4B) is in qualitative agreement with the theoretical prediction (Figure 3D).
evidence: Comparison between data and model

claim: The step-like shape of the RNAP loading rate agrees with previous measurements performed on the same reporter construct.
source: The step-like shape of the RNAP loading rate (Figure 4C, blue points) agrees with previous measurements performed on this same reporter construct (Garcia et al., 2013).
evidence: Comparison with prior work with citation

claim: The thermodynamic MWC model without mitotic repression produced transcriptional onset times that were much lower than those experimentally observed.
source: Although the model accounted for the initial rate of RNAP loading (Figure 4C, blue line), it produced transcriptional onset times that were much lower than those that we experimentally observed (Appendix 1—figure 6B, purple line).
evidence: Discrepancy between model and data

claim: The disagreement between model and data for onset times was hypothesized to be due to the model not accounting for mitotic repression.
source: We hypothesized that this disagreement was due to our model not accounting for mitotic repression, when the transcriptional machinery appears to be silent immediately after cell division (Shermoen and O'Farrell, 1991; Gottesfeld and Forbes, 1997; Parsons and Spencer, 1997; Garcia et al., 2013).
evidence: Hypothesis based on known biological phenomenon with citations

claim: All embryos from zelda germline clone mothers lack maternally deposited Zelda.
source: All embryos from these mothers lack maternally deposited Zelda; female embryos still have a functional copy of zelda from their father, but this copy is not transcribed until after the maternal-to-zygotic transition, during nuclear cycle 14 (Liang et al., 2008).
evidence: Description of genetic system with citation

claim: The absence of Zelda did not have a substantial effect on the spatiotemporal pattern of Bicoid.
source: We confirmed that the absence of Zelda did not have a substantial effect on the spatiotemporal pattern of Bicoid (Appendix section 4; Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: Experimental observation with citation

claim: Close to 100% of nuclei in wild-type embryos exhibited transcription along the length of the embryo.
source: While close to 100% of nuclei in wild-type embryos exhibited transcription along the length of the embryo (Figure 4E, blue; Video 5), measurements in the zelda− background revealed that some nuclei never displayed any transcription during the entire nuclear cycle (Video 6).
evidence: Experimental observation from data

claim: In zelda-deficient embryos, some nuclei never displayed any transcription during the entire nuclear cycle.
source: While close to 100% of nuclei in wild-type embryos exhibited transcription along the length of the embryo (Figure 4E, blue; Video 5), measurements in the zelda− background revealed that some nuclei never displayed any transcription during the entire nuclear cycle (Video 6).
evidence: Experimental observation from data

claim: In zelda-deficient embryos, transcription occurred only in the anterior part of the embryo, with transcription disappearing completely in positions posterior to about 40% of the embryo length.
source: Specifically, transcription occurred only in the anterior part of the embryo, with transcription disappearing completely in positions posterior to about 40% of the embryo length (Figure 4E, red).
evidence: Experimental observation from data

claim: RNAP loading rates in zelda-deficient embryos were comparable to the corresponding rates in wild-type embryos.
source: Interestingly, these RNAP loading rates were comparable to the corresponding rates in wild-type embryos (Figure 4C, red points).
evidence: Comparison of experimental data

claim: Removing Zelda primarily results in a delay of transcription with only negligible effects on the underlying rates of RNAP loading.
source: Together, these observations indicated that removing Zelda primarily results in a delay of transcription with only negligible effects on the underlying rates of RNAP loading, consistent with previous fixed-embryo experiments (Nien et al., 2011; Foo et al., 2014) and with recent live-imaging measurements in which Zelda binding was reduced at specific enhancers (Dufourt et al., 2018; Yamada et al., 2019).
evidence: Interpretation of data consistent with prior work with citations

claim: The thermodynamic MWC model could not account for the lack of transcriptional activity posterior to 40% of the embryo length in the zelda-deficient mutant.
source: Further, our model could not account for the lack of transcriptional activity posterior to 40% of the embryo length in the zelda− mutant (Figure 4E, red).
evidence: Discrepancy between model and data

claim: The discrepancies between model and data suggest that the thermodynamic MWC model cannot fully describe the transcriptional regulation of the hunchback promoter by Bicoid and Zelda.
source: These discrepancies suggest that the thermodynamic MWC model cannot fully describe the transcriptional regulation of the hunchback promoter by Bicoid and Zelda.
evidence: Conclusion from model-data comparison

claim: The thermodynamic MWC model is not sufficient to explain the regulation of hunchback by Bicoid and Zelda.
source: We concluded that our thermodynamic MWC model is not sufficient to explain the regulation of hunchback by Bicoid and Zelda.
evidence: Conclusion from systematic model testing

claim: The generalized thermodynamic model also failed to explain the zelda-deficient data.
source: The generalized thermodynamic model also failed to explain the zelda− data (Appendix section 6.2; Figure 5C, yellow).
evidence: Result from systematic parameter exploration

claim: No thermodynamic model of Bicoid-activated hunchback transcription can predict transcriptional onset in the absence of Zelda.
source: Nevertheless, our results strongly suggest that no thermodynamic model of Bicoid-activated hunchback transcription can predict transcriptional onset in the absence of Zelda, casting doubt on the general applicability of these models to transcriptional regulation in development.
evidence: Conclusion from systematic exploration of model space

claim: Thermodynamic models assume that the system responds instantaneously to any changes in input transcription factor concentration.
source: The thermodynamic models investigated in this work have assumed that the system responds instantaneously to any changes in input transcription factor concentration.
evidence: Description of model assumption

claim: Since Bicoid and Zelda are imported into the nucleus by around 3 min into the nuclear cycle, thermodynamic models predict that transcription will ensue at approximately that time.
source: As a result, since Bicoid and Zelda are imported into the nucleus by around 3 min into the nuclear cycle (Figure 3A and B), these models always predict that transcription will ensue at approximately that time.
evidence: Inference from model assumptions and data

claim: Zelda has been implicated in the acetylation of chromatin, a histone modification that renders nucleosomes unstable and increases DNA accessibility.
source: Specifically, Zelda has been implicated in the acetylation of chromatin, a histone modification that renders nucleosomes unstable and increases DNA accessibility (Li et al., 2014a; Li and Eisen, 2018).
evidence: Summary of prior work with citations

claim: Bicoid has been shown to interact with the co-activator dCBP, which possesses histone acetyltransferase activity.
source: Further, Bicoid has been shown to interact with the co-activator dCBP, which possesses histone acetyltransferase activity (Fu et al., 2004).
evidence: Summary of prior work with citation

claim: Recent studies have proposed the existence of multiple transcriptionally silent steps that the promoter needs to transition through before transcriptional onset.
source: Additionally, recent studies by Desponds et al., 2016 in hunchback and by Dufourt et al., 2018 in snail have proposed the existence of multiple transcriptionally silent steps that the promoter needs to transition through before transcriptional onset.
evidence: Summary of prior work with citations

claim: The transcriptionally silent steps could correspond to the recruitment of histone modifiers, nucleosome remodelers, and the transcriptional machinery, or to the step-wise unraveling of discrete histone-DNA contacts.
source: These steps could correspond to, for example, the recruitment of histone modifiers, nucleosome remodelers, and the transcriptional machinery (Li et al., 2014a; Park et al., 2019), or to the step-wise unraveling of discrete histone-DNA contacts (Culkin et al., 2017).
evidence: Speculation based on cited literature

claim: Zelda plays a role in modulating the number of intermediate steps and their transition rates.
source: Further, Dufourt et al., 2018 proposed that Zelda plays a role in modulating the number of these steps and their transition rates.
evidence: Summary of prior work with citation

claim: In the transcription-factor-driven chromatin accessibility model, the system slowly and irreversibly transitions through m transcriptionally silent states before DNA becomes accessible and transcription ensues.
source: We therefore proposed a model of transcription-factor-driven chromatin accessibility in which, in order for the DNA to become accessible and transcription to ensue, the system slowly and irreversibly transitions through m transcriptionally silent states (Appendix section 8.1; Figure 7A).
evidence: Description of proposed model

claim: The transitions between transcriptionally silent states can be catalyzed by the presence of Bicoid and Zelda.
source: Finally, in a stark deviation from the MWC framework, we posit that these transitions can be catalyzed by the presence of Bicoid and Zelda
evidence: Key feature of proposed model

claim: The timing of transcriptional output in the transcription-factor-driven model arose directly from the model's initial irreversible transitions.
source: Instead, the timing of transcriptional output arose directly from the model's initial irreversible transitions (Appendix 1—figure 14), obviating the need for an arbitrary suppression window in the beginning of the nuclear cycle.
evidence: Explanation of model behavior

claim: The transcription-factor-driven chromatin accessibility model encompasses a much larger region of parameter space than the thermodynamic and non-equilibrium MWC models.
source: Finally, note that this model encompasses a much larger region of parameter space than the thermodynamic and non-equilibrium MWC models and, as expected from the agreement between model and experiment described above, contained both the wild-type and zelda− data points within its domain (Figure 7D).
evidence: Comparison of model capabilities

claim: The hunchback P2 minimal enhancer provides a unique opportunity to dissect the relative contribution of chromatin regulation on transcriptional dynamics.
source: However, the hunchback P2 minimal enhancer provides a unique opportunity to dissect the relative contribution of chromatin regulation on transcriptional dynamics because, in the early embryo, chromatin accessibility at hunchback is granted by both Bicoid and Zelda (Hannon et al., 2017).
evidence: Justification for experimental system with citation

claim: The degree of hunchback transcriptional activity is regulated directly by Bicoid.
source: The degree of hunchback transcriptional activity, however, is regulated directly by Bicoid (Driever and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1989; Driever et al., 1989; Struhl et al., 1989).
evidence: Summary of prior work with citations

claim: Genetic elimination of Zelda function interferes with acquisition of full chromatin accessibility, but the hunchback locus retains a measurable degree of accessibility and transcriptional activity stemming from Bicoid function.
source: Therefore, while genetic elimination of Zelda function interferes with acquisition of full chromatin accessibility, the hunchback locus retains a measurable degree of accessibility and transcriptional activity stemming from Bicoid function, allowing for a quantitative determination of the contribution of Zelda-dependent chromatin accessibility on the transcriptional dynamics of the locus.
evidence: Justification for experimental approach

claim: The study introduced a novel approach that incorporated transient dynamics of input transcription-factor concentrations in order to predict the instantaneous output transcriptional dynamics of hunchback.
source: As a result, we went beyond widespread steady-state descriptions of development and introduced a novel approach that incorporated transient dynamics of input transcription-factor concentrations in order to predict the instantaneous output transcriptional dynamics of hunchback (Figure 3C).
evidence: Description of methodological contribution

claim: The thermodynamic MWC model sufficiently predicts the timing of the onset of transcription and the subsequent initial rate of RNAP loading as a function of Bicoid and Zelda concentration in wild-type embryos.
source: This approach revealed that the thermodynamic MWC model sufficiently predicts the timing of the onset of transcription and the subsequent initial rate of RNAP loading as a function of Bicoid and Zelda concentration.
evidence: Result from model-data comparison

claim: At the early stages of development analyzed, an unknown transcription factor regulating hunchback would need to be both maternally provided and patterned in a spatial gradient to produce the observed position-dependent transcriptional onset times.
source: However, at the early stages of development analyzed here, such a factor would need to be both maternally provided and patterned in a spatial gradient to produce the observed position-dependent transcriptional onset times.
evidence: Logical inference about what would be required

claim: None of the known maternal genes regulate the expression of the hunchback reporter in a fashion that would produce position-dependent transcriptional onset times.
source: To our knowledge, none of the known maternal genes regulate the expression of this hunchback reporter in such a fashion (Chen et al., 2012; Perry et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement about lack of evidence with citations

claim: The MWC thermodynamic model cannot accurately predict hunchback transcriptional dynamics.
source: We conclude that the MWC thermodynamic model cannot accurately predict hunchback transcriptional dynamics.
evidence: Conclusion from systematic model testing

claim: A successful non-equilibrium MWC model with more than five Bicoid-binding sites would probably operate near the limits of its explanatory power.
source: While we were unable to investigate models with more than five Bicoid-binding sites due to computational complexity (Estrada et al., 2016), the substantial distance in parameter space between the mutant data and the investigated models (Figure 6B) suggested that a successful model with more than five Bicoid-binding sites would probably operate near the limits of its explanatory power, similar to the conclusions from studies that explored hunchback regulation under the steady-state assumption (Park et al., 2019).
evidence: Inference from parameter exploration with citation

claim: The observed transcriptional onset times could not be described by any previously proposed thermodynamic MWC mechanism of chromatin accessibility, or even by a more generic non-equilibrium MWC model in which energy is continuously dissipated.
source: Thus, despite the simplicity and success of the MWC model in predicting the effects of protein allostery in a wide range of biological contexts (Keymer et al., 2006; Swem et al., 2008; Martins and Swain, 2011; Marzen et al., 2013; Rapp and Yifrach, 2017; Razo-Mejia et al., 2018; Chure et al., 2019; Rapp and Yifrach, 2019), the observed transcriptional onset times could not be described by any previously proposed thermodynamic MWC mechanism of chromatin accessibility, or even by a more generic non-equilibrium MWC model in which energy is continuously dissipated (Tu, 2008; Kim and O'Shea, 2008; Narula and Igoshin, 2010; Estrada et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: Conclusion from systematic model testing with citations

claim: Both Bicoid and Zelda actively drive DNA accessibility.
source: Since Zelda is associated with histone acetylation, which is correlated with increased chromatin accessibility (Li et al., 2014a; Li and Eisen, 2018), and Bicoid interacts with the co-activator dCBP, which has histone acetyltransferase activity (Fu et al., 2004; Fu and Ma, 2005; Park et al., 2019), we suspect that both Bicoid and Zelda actively drive DNA accessibility.
evidence: Inference from cited literature

claim: A molecular pathway shared by Bicoid and Zelda to render chromatin accessible is consistent with the results and with recent genome-wide experiments showing that Bicoid can rescue the function of Zelda-dependent enhancers at high enough concentrations.
source: A molecular pathway shared by Bicoid and Zelda to render chromatin accessible is consistent with our results, and with recent genome-wide experiments showing that Bicoid can rescue the function of Zelda-dependent enhancers at high enough concentrations (Hannon et al., 2017).
evidence: Interpretation consistent with data and cited work

claim: The binding of Bicoid and Zelda may trigger a set of molecular events that locks DNA into an accessible state.
source: Thus, the binding of Bicoid and Zelda, rather than just biasing the equilibrium toward the open chromatin state as in the MWC mechanism, may trigger a set of molecular events that locks DNA into an accessible state.
evidence: Proposed mechanism based on data interpretation

claim: Recent work dissecting the transcriptional onset time distribution of snail suggested the existence of three intermediate steps.
source: Interestingly, recent work dissecting the transcriptional onset time distribution of snail also suggested the existence of three such intermediate steps in the context of that gene (Dufourt et al., 2018).
evidence: Summary of prior work with citation

claim: The removal and addition of Zelda modulates the timing of transcriptional onset of sog and snail.
source: Given that, as in hunchback, the removal and addition of Zelda modulates the timing of transcriptional onset of sog and snail (Dufourt et al., 2018; Yamada et al., 2019), we speculate that transcription-factor-driven chromatin accessibility may also be at play in these pathways.
evidence: Summary of prior work with citations

claim: Transcription-factor-driven chromatin accessibility may be at play in the regulation of sog and snail.
source: Given that, as in hunchback, the removal and addition of Zelda modulates the timing of transcriptional onset of sog and snail (Dufourt et al., 2018; Yamada et al., 2019), we speculate that transcription-factor-driven chromatin accessibility may also be at play in these pathways.
evidence: Speculation based on similarity to current findings

claim: The results strongly suggest that chromatin state does not fluctuate thermodynamically, but rather progresses through a series of stepwise, transcription-factor-driven transitions into a final RNAP-accessible configuration.
source: Thus, taken in consideration with similar works examining the dynamics of transcription onset (Desponds et al., 2016; Dufourt et al., 2018; Fritzsch et al., 2018; Li et al., 2018), our results strongly suggest that chromatin state does not fluctuate thermodynamically, but rather progresses through a series of stepwise, transcription-factor-driven transitions into a final RNAP-accessible configuration (Coulon et al., 2013).
evidence: Conclusion from data and comparison with cited literature

claim: Accounting for intermediate states obviates the need for the ad hoc imposition of a mitotic repression window.
source: Intriguingly, accounting for these intermediate states also obviated the need for the ad hoc imposition of a mitotic repression window (Appendix sections 3 and 8.1), which was required in the thermodynamic MWC model (Appendix 1—figure 6).
evidence: Comparison of model features

claim: The results suggest a mechanistic interpretation of the phenomenon of mitotic repression after anaphase, where the promoter must traverse through intermediary transcriptionally silent states before transcriptional onset can occur.
source: Our results thus suggest a mechanistic interpretation of the phenomenon of mitotic repression after anaphase, where the promoter must traverse through intermediary transcriptionally silent states before transcriptional onset can occur.
evidence: Interpretation of model implications

claim: The regulatory action of Bicoid and Zelda was revealed by utilizing the dynamic information provided by live imaging to analyze the transient nature of the transcriptional onset time.
source: Here, we revealed the regulatory action of Bicoid and Zelda by utilizing the dynamic information provided by live imaging to analyze the transient nature of the transcriptional onset time, highlighting the need for descriptions of development that go beyond steady state and acknowledge the highly dynamic changes in transcription-factor concentrations that drive developmental programs.
evidence: Summary of methodological approach and its value

claim: Other models may have comparable explanatory power to the transcription-factor-driven chromatin accessibility model.
source: While we showed that one model incorporating transcription-factor-driven chromatin accessibility could recapitulate hunchback transcriptional regulation by Bicoid and Zelda, and is consistent with molecular evidence on the modes of action of these transcription factors, other models may have comparable explanatory power.
evidence: Acknowledgment of alternative possibilities

claim: A systematic exploration of different classes of models and their unique predictions will identify measurements that determine which specific model is the most appropriate description of transcriptional regulation in development.
source: In the future, a systematic exploration of different classes of models and their unique predictions will identify measurements that determine which specific model is the most appropriate description of transcriptional regulation in development and how it is implemented at the molecular level.
evidence: Proposal for future work

claim: Detailed studies of single-cell features of transcriptional dynamics such as the distribution of transcriptional onset times could shed light on chromatin-regulating mechanisms.
source: While all the analyses in this work relied on mean levels of input concentrations and output transcription levels, detailed studies of single-cell features of transcriptional dynamics such as the distribution of transcriptional onset times (Narula and Igoshin, 2010; Dufourt et al., 2018; Fritzsch et al., 2018) could shed light on these chromatin-regulating mechanisms.
evidence: Proposal for future work with citations

claim: Simultaneous measurement of local transcription-factor concentrations at sites of transcription and of transcriptional initiation with high spatiotemporal resolution could provide further information about chromatin accessibility dynamics.
source: Simultaneous measurement of local transcription-factor concentrations at sites of transcription and of transcriptional initiation with high spatiotemporal resolution, such as afforded by lattice light-sheet microscopy (Mir et al., 2018), could provide further information about chromatin accessibility dynamics.
evidence: Proposal for future work with citation

claim: Different theoretical models may make distinct predictions about the effect of modulating the number, placement, and affinity of Bicoid and Zelda sites in the hunchback enhancer.
source: Finally, different theoretical models may make distinct predictions about the effect of modulating the number, placement, and affinity of Bicoid and Zelda sites (and even of nucleosomes) in the hunchback enhancer.
evidence: Proposal for future work

claim: Bicoid and Zelda actively drive chromatin accessibility, possibly through histone acetylation.
source: At least regarding the activation of hunchback, and likely similar developmental genes such as snail and sog (Dufourt et al., 2018; Yamada et al., 2019), we speculate that Bicoid and Zelda actively drive chromatin accessibility, possibly through histone acetylation.
evidence: Speculation based on data and cited literature

claim: Once chromatin becomes accessible, thermodynamic models can predict hunchback transcription without the need to invoke energy expenditure and non-equilibrium models.
source: Once chromatin becomes accessible, thermodynamic models can predict hunchback transcription without the need to invoke energy expenditure and non-equilibrium models.
evidence: Conclusion from model fitting

claim: The dialogue between theoretical models and the experimental testing of their predictions at high spatiotemporal resolution is a powerful tool for biological discovery.
source: Regardless of whether we have identified the only possible model of chromatin accessibility and regulation, we have demonstrated that this dialogue between theoretical models and the experimental testing of their predictions at high spatiotemporal resolution is a powerful tool for biological discovery.
evidence: Reflection on methodological approach

claim: The new insights afforded by the theory-experiment dialogue will refine theoretical descriptions of transcriptional regulation as a further step toward a predictive understanding of cellular decision-making in development.
source: The new insights afforded by this dialogue will undoubtedly refine theoretical descriptions of transcriptional regulation as a further step toward a predictive understanding of cellular decision-making in development.
evidence: Statement about broader impact

claim: Zelda-binding sites in the hunchback promoter were identified as heptamers scoring three or higher using a Zelda alignment matrix.
source: Zelda-binding sites in the hunchback promoter were identified as heptamers scoring three or higher using a Zelda alignment matrix (Harrison et al., 2011) and the Advanced PASTER entry form online (http://stormo.wustl.edu/consensus/cgi-bin/Server/Interface/patser.cgi) (Hertz et al., 1990; Hertz and Stormo, 1999).
evidence: Description of computational method with citations

claim: All embryos lacking maternally deposited Zelda showed aberrant morphology in nuclear size and shape.
source: All embryos lacking maternally deposited Zelda showed aberrant morphology in nuclear size and shape (data not shown), as previously reported (Liang et al., 2008; Staudt et al., 2006).
evidence: Experimental observation with citations
